findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:288 — Light-theme value changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 70%, reversing intended emphasis; preserve 30% for light themes and use the corresponding dark-theme secondary value.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:519 — `.name` light-theme color changed from `$primary` at 30% lightness to 50%, altering the existing light-theme appearance instead of only adding a dark-theme alternative.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` reverses the original 70% light-theme value to 30% and uses 70% for dark themes, opposite the equivalent desktop rule and overly prominent in light themes.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:179 — Topic preview `h3` loses its original 20% light-theme value and changes to 50%; it should match the desktop 20%/80% light/dark mapping.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:494 — `.name` changes from the original 30% light-theme value to 50%, causing an unintended mobile light-theme visual regression.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:179 — Topic preview `h3` loses its original 20% light-theme value and changes to 50%; it should match the desktop 20%/80% light/dark mapping.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff for mobile/topic-post.scss line 179, the h3 color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the light-theme value from 20% to 50%, which is inconsistent. Comparing to desktop/topic-post.scss line 321, the h3 uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, maintaining the original 20% for light theme. The mobile version should use 20%/80% to match desktop, not 50%/50%.
